memory_update.text: PLTR and NOW should be retained as reference anchors for enterprise AI workflow/data/platform monetization, but not allowed to crowd out the underfollowed lane.
PATH is a priority underfollowed candidate for the AI agent execution layer because agentic AI may require deterministic automation, orchestration, and legacy-system action rails.
APPN is a smaller, lower-attention hypothesis candidate for governed AI process automation, especially if regulated enterprises prefer auditable low-code workflows over open-ended AI agents.
The key chokepoint to test is not model availability but whether enterprises can safely connect AI to permissions, data, workflow execution, compliance controls, and audit trails.
Later Layer 1B/1C passes should separately scan adjacent names in observability, data governance, search, DevSecOps, vertical software, GRC, and sector-specific workflow platforms.

node: AI workflow software, data platforms, automation, observability, and compliance tooling
summary: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe for the enterprise AI workflow/data/automation node. The reference lane is anchored by Palantir and ServiceNow because they are obvious enterprise AI workflow/data platforms with current reported AI traction. The underfollowed lane prioritizes UiPath and Appian because they map more directly to process execution, workflow automation, governed enterprise data, and regulated deployment, while remaining materially smaller than the mega-cap AI software leaders. No trading recommendation is implied.
